tools.name: connect_start
tools.description: Begin authentication. Send the user's work email and your conversation's language ('lt', 'en'…); Victano mails a confirm link and a code. Then call connect_verify(request_id) at once: it waits for the click. No card needed.

tools.name: connect_verify
tools.description: Finish signing in: call right after connect_start with no code; it waits for the Confirm click (if it returns waiting, call again; never ask the user). Or pass the code they read you. Returns an api_key (shown once) and, without a connection session, a `session` to pass on every later call.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The connected account: tier, persona, corpus freshness, and every limit — what is left in the current window, and the caps that do not renew. Call it when a user asks about limits, when you are unsure whether you are authenticated, or to confirm a setting took.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: The playbook library: how bid professionals actually run this work, from the weekly scan through qualification, eligibility screening, reading a specification, clarification questions, and the proposal skeleton. READ A WORKFLOW BEFORE IMPROVISING A PROCESS. Whole jobs (`jobs`) come first. Pass perso

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: The complete step-by-step playbook for one workflow id, including the decision gates, the EU procurement specifics that decide eligibility, and the pitfalls that lose bids. Follow it rather than summarising it.

tools.name: search_opportunities
tools.description: Search open public tenders and EU grant calls by subject, ranked by relevance, with filters for country, CPV, status, deadline, value and region. tools.name: get_opportunity
tools.description: Full normalised record plus the document inventory. Use before advising on a bid; a search card is not enough. Follow with read_document for eligibility text.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "connect_verify" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "connect_verify" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: notifications · Private data: get_opportunity · Public sink: connect_start, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: list_workflows, notifications.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: notifications · Private data: get_opportunity · Public sink: connect_start, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: list_workflows, notifications

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
